title: Never Step Over a Digging Stick

collection.credit: NEW EVENTS — LUCK, OMENS AND LAVASTONES (LO-01 to LO-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)

ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)

collection.description: A villager watches in horror as a friend steps over a digging stick, which is said to be bad luck.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) was taught as a child never to step over a digging stick lying on the ground: it's bad luck, and the garden won't grow. (friend) has never heard of this, and has just stepped over (subject)'s digging stick, twice, without a thought. (subject) is staring at (friend.him/her) in horror.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (subject) explains. (friend) listens politely, then steps back over the stick a third time, to "undo it." "That's not how it works," says (subject). "How does it work, then?" (subject) realizes (subject.he/she) has no idea. They spend the afternoon inventing rules for undoing it. The garden, as it happens, grows perfectly well.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) says nothing. When (friend) has gone, (subject.he/she) picks up the stick, turns it round three times, and puts it down again, the way (subject.his/her) grandmother did. Is that a real fix? (subject) doesn't know. It makes (subject.him/her) feel better, though, and that's worth something.
